pool.text: Analyzing the \( xy \)-plane, the line \( y = 2x - c \) and the parabola \( y = x^2 + 3 \) intersect at exactly one point, where \( c \) is a constant. What is the value of \( c \)?
pool.sol: Set \( x^2 + 3 = 2x - c \): \( x^2 - 2x + (c + 3) = 0 \). One intersection means the discriminant is 0: \( 4 - 4(c + 3) = 0 \), so \( c = -2 \).

pool.text: Suppose the equation \( x^2 + y^2 + 10x - 6y - 2 = 0 \) defines a circle in the \( xy \)-plane. What is the radius of the circle?
pool.sol: Completing the square: \( (x + 5)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 36 \), so the radius is 6.

pool.text: Notice that the graph of \( y = -(x + 2)(x - 2) \) intersects the \( x \)-axis at the points \( (p, 0) \) and \( (q, 0) \). What is the value of \( q - p \), where \( q > p \)?
pool.sol: The \( x \)-intercepts are -2 and 2, so \( q - p = 2 - (-2) = 4 \).
